themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. All three models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative marketing content governance all three models say deciding whether evidence supports a claim is contextual judgment, with Claude noting expert reviewers disagree, ChatGPT pointing to jurisdiction and audience, and Gemini saying probabilistic models cannot do it; the same semantic problem drives the governed semantic context layer.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing you measure often shifts while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization has no stable unit or click to attribute, identity resolution has no natural signal that a link was wrong, B2B buying-group intent has almost no confirmed outcomes, and content governance reviewers themselves disagree on the right call.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and force everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: For safe agent execution all three models put a proxy or gateway in front of every write with hard spend and audience caps, consent enforcement gets a single egress gate, journey orchestration gets one shared contact ledger and pre-send check, and content governance gets an approved-claims library that limits what tools may say.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: Agent traffic work keeps returning to agents that profit from looking human and no one with leverage to issue credentials, the semantic context layer is called a political settlement wearing a data modeling costume, journey orchestration fails because channel P&Ls reward saying yes, and incrementality stalls because platforms have no reason to expose treatment logs.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. Compliance and effects can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models agree enforcement ends at the boundary of systems you do not control, answer engines expose no ranking or retrieval logs, and incrementality suffers because platforms control both delivery and the evidence.
